To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

students who volunteer to take part in a study of prison behavior score higher than students volunteering for a study without any mention of prison life on a variety of scales measuring dispositions related to abusive behavior and that the SPE was not a "true experiment" in the sense that the researchers did not randomly assign students to the prisoner and guard groups, but rather selected students for these groups on the basis of their responses to a questionnaire.

participants in a study of prison guards scored significantly higher on the abuse-related dis-positions of aggressiveness and authoritarianism and significantly lower on the nonabuse-related disposition of empathy than did participants in a control study.
participants who volunteered to participate in a psychological study of life in prison were significantly more likely to have the personality characteristics associated with abusive behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the Stanford Prison Experiment was a situationist experiment or a person x situation interactionist experiment.
the question of whether the participants in the SPE (Haney, Banks & Zimbardo,1973) were selected to take part in the study based on their dispositions to behave in an abusively aggressive manner.

the question of whether the participants who volunteered to be guards in the Stanford Prison experiment (Haney et al., 1973; Zimbardo, Haney, Banks, & Jaffee, 1973; hereafter SPE) had a disposition toward behaving abusively toward others.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SPE was a classic example of a situationist effect.
, although the SPE is a very powerful study, there are some important limitations that should be taken into account in the interpretation of the results.
the Stanford Prison Experiment, and the Abu Ghraib prison abuse scandal, are both the result of the interaction of situational and personal factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the SPE was not simply a demonstration of the effects of a situation on human behavior, but that it was also a demonstration of how people who volunteer for studies of human behavior are likely to differ on important personality traits that can influence their behavior in that setting.
the SPE was an experiment in person-situation interactions, not just a situationist experiment.
the SPE participants who volunteered to be guards were not simply "good kids" who went bad.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPE was not a situationist demonstration of the power of a situation to transform people.
the participants in the Stanford Prison experiment did not represent the general population.
we should not be surprised by abusive behavior when people are put in positions of power over others.
